**1. The Act is in force; staggered application is underway**

- The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) formally entered into force on August 1, 2024.([digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai?utm_source=openai))

**2. Major post‑report change: the “Digital Omnibus” delayed high‑risk deadlines**

Since the GIRAI 2026 dataset was cut (July 7, 2026), a key change is that the EU has *officially* shifted the main high‑risk AI timelines:

- The “Digital Omnibus on AI” (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744), adopted in July 2026, amends the AI Act to “simplify and streamline” implementation and adjusts the application dates for high‑risk rules.([eur-lex.europa.eu](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A32026R1744&utm_source=openai))  
- Original plan: many high‑risk AI obligations were due to apply on August 2, 2026.([digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai?utm_source=openai))  
- New plan (now law):  
  - Stand‑alone high‑risk AI systems (Annex III): obligations now apply from **December 2, 2027**.([consilium.europa.eu](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/policies/artificial-intelligence-act/timeline-artificial-intelligence/?utm_source=openai))  
  - High‑risk AI systems embedded in products covered by sectoral safety rules (Annex I): obligations now apply from **August 2, 2028**.([consilium.europa.eu](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/policies/artificial-intelligence-act/timeline-artificial-intelligence/?utm_source=openai))  
- The EU Council and Parliament framed this as necessary because standards, guidance and national authorities would not be ready for the original August 2026 date.([eur-lex.europa.eu](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A32026R1744&utm_source=openai))  

For GIRAI users: this means that, although the Act is “live” as of August 2, 2026, the *heaviest* compliance burden for high‑risk systems has been pushed back by roughly 16–24 months.

Despite those delays, several obligations either already apply or start this summer:

- **Prohibited AI practices** (e.g. certain forms of social scoring, manipulative systems) had an early application date; they were among the first provisions to apply after entry into force.([digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai?utm_source=openai))

The AI Act Service Desk FAQ notes that providers of the “most advanced models” had a one‑year transition (Aug 2, 2025–Aug 2, 2026) before enforcement powers fully kick in.([ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/faq?utm_source=openai))  
- **Article 50 (“synthetic content” / transparency for AI‑generated content):**  
  - Article 50 obligations (e.g. marking AI‑generated or manipulated content, including some chatbot disclosure rules) are among the provisions applying in 2026, and there’s a transitional deadline for systems already on the market before August 2, 2026, to come into line with Article 50(2).([ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline?utm_source=openai))  
  - Tech press this week is emphasising that, despite high‑risk delays, the Act’s chatbot and content‑transparency rules “apply this week” (i.e. around August 2, 2026), so customer‑facing AI tools in Europe now face concrete transparency duties.([techradar.com](https://www.techradar.com/pro/celebrating-the-ai-act-delay-the-eu-ai-acts-chatbot-and-content-rules-apply-this-week?utm_source=openai))  

**4. New enforcement and support structures**

- The **European AI Office** (the central enforcement and coordination body under the Act) has been moving from set‑up to operational mode through 2025–26; the Commission has also announced calls to build up EU‑level model‑evaluation capacity before systems hit the market.([digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai?utm_source=openai))  
- The Commission and Council stress that the Digital Omnibus changes are meant to avoid legal uncertainty and uneven enforcement by aligning high‑risk deadlines with the readiness of standards and national authorities.([digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act?utm_source=openai))  

**5. Why this matters for interpreting GIRAI 2026**

- GIRAI 2026 treats the EU AI Act as *adopted but still in staged implementation*. Country scores for EU members reflect the existence and design of this framework, plus any national measures, *at the time of data generation* (July 7, 2026).
